correctness.rationale: The first chosen winner and next chosen winner yield only two nonabsorbed branches (m,k) and (m-1,k+1), with weights (k-1)/m and k(m-k)/[m(k+1)] for k>=2, and then unbiased two-player ruin on 0..m+k. Boundary k=0 absorbs at time1; k=1 has first-step absorption 1/m; k=m omits second branch. Solving the discrete harmonic ruin PGF yields the claimed cosh formula and exact mean 2+k(m-2)+k^2/m for k>=2, E tau=m for k=1. For k/m->alpha>0 the Laplace transform converges to Brownian first-exit with generator (1/2)d²/dx². For sparse k=o(m), the killed sine series must control high negative eigenvalue modes as the proof explicitly does; dominated convergence yields Phi(t) and the mixture weights yield the m/k prefactor. Reflection principle plus half-line survival bound shows tau/(mk)->0 and Tonelli gives ∫Phi=1. Independent direct unreduced rational Markov simulation matched ruin-mixture survival for every m=2..6, k=0..m, t=0..10; finite checks are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The exact hitting-time law resolves a concrete transition case raised in the motivating primary paper. Its sparse-excess mean mk is dominated by rare m²-scale trajectories even though the typical duration divided by mk converges to zero. The explicit theta-series rare tail and all-m,k finite law are useful natural invariants, not mere simulation improvements.

final_claim: For m>=2 and 0<=k<=m, simple sticky walks started with k two-card and m-k one-card players have exact two-round-conditioned gambler-ruin mixture law for all finite absorption-time probabilities and generating functions; when 1<=k=o(m), E tau~mk yet tau/(mk)->0 in probability and (m/k)P(tau>floor(t*m^2))->Phi(t)=4 sum_{j>=0} exp(-((2j+1)^2 pi^2/2)*t) for each fixed t>0.
limitations: Finite initial holdings exactly one or two, uniform current-active winner; all m>=2.
Brownian limit assumes k/m->alpha in (0,1]; sparse-tail limit holds only each t>0 with k=o(m).
Finite experiments are not an infinite proof; stronger inaccessible literature may exist.
